description: 2 tactical challenges for White in the Tarrasch Trap. Punish 8...g6?? with the double attack 10.Qc4!.

drills.briefExplanation: 9.Nxc6 bxc6 10.Qc4! — win the bishop with a double attack on c6 and f7.
drills.description: White to play. Black weakened with 8...g6?? — strike with 9.Nxc6!.
drills.explanation: The Tarrasch Trap: after 8...g6?? Black's kingside is airy, and 9.Nxc6 bxc6 10.Qc4! is the punishment — the queen attacks the c6 bishop and eyes f7 in one move. Black can't defend both: 10...d5 11.Qxc6+ wins the bishop, and 10...Be6 11.Qxe6+ fxe6 leaves Black's structure in ruins. Provoking ...g6 was the whole idea.
drills.name: The Double Attack

drills.briefExplanation: 8.Nxd4 g6?? 9.Nxc6 bxc6 10.Qc4! — the full trap from the recapture.
drills.description: White to play. Black took on d4 — recapture and set the trap.
drills.explanation: The trap in full sequence: 8.Nxd4 centralizes, and after the weakening 8...g6?? White executes 9.Nxc6 bxc6 10.Qc4!. Note the move order matters — White provokes ...g6 before striking, because the double attack needs the f7 weakness to be decisive. Patience in trap-setting is a skill.
drills.name: Setting the Trap
